title: Consolidate retry/deadline semantics, client idempotency, and hedging defaults across runtime + SDKs
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: Multiple services and SDKs expose different retry/backoff and deadline semantics. Some clients use naive exponential backoff, others rely on hedged requests; idempotency headers are inconsistently applied, causing duplicate side-effects in Dedicated and Private deployments during partial failover. This leads to SLO violations and customer-facing errors during multi-region failovers and sudden load spikes.

Goal: Define a single 'retry contract' that spans server runtime and official SDKs: clear deadline propagation, default retry/backoff profiles by route class, opt-in hedging with a configurable hedge-window, and a canonical idempotency key format to allow safe retries and hedged requests. Provide a migration path and rollout with telemetry and circuit-breaker integration so we can load-shed gracefully under overload and keep tail latency within SLOs.

Scope: runtime (kernel selection + request router), hosted API, official SDKs (python/js/go), console rollout controls, and docs. Excludes: third-party partner SDKs (will provide compatibility guidance).

Design summary:
- Deadline propagation: clients may send X-Redwood-Deadline-ms; runtime enforces and translates to per-model token budget. Servers must reject requests when remaining deadline < 20ms.
- Retry policy surface: routes labeled 'idempotent-by-default' (embeddings, rerank) get safe retries up to 2 attempts; 'stateful' routes (fine-tune, admin) default to no automatic server-side retry. The SDKs expose RetryPolicy objects and a single default: "balanced" (initial 20ms jitter, exponential backoff factor 2, max interval 500ms, overall attempt cap 3).
- Hedge window: hedging is opt-in per-request via Hedge-Mode header. Default SDK behavior: hedging disabled. For low-latency routes we provide an explicit HedgePolicy: start a speculative second request at t = max(1.2 * p50_latency, 35ms) if first request hasn't started streaming. Hedge responses are deduped via canonical idempotency key.
- Idempotency key: canonical header: Idempotency-Key. SDKs will generate V2 keys: prefix "rid-v2-" + base64(uuid+client-ts+SIG). Servers verify format but accept older keys. Keys should be stored in the runtime KV cache with 24h TTL for dedupe.
- Circuit breakers & load shedding: add a per-route token-bucket-based shedder that consults runtime queue length, GPU availability, and per-customer SLA. When shed, server returns 429 with Retry-After and 'X-Redwood-Shed-Reason' header. SDKs should interpret 429 as non-fatal for idempotent routes and may queue a single retry subject to backoff and remaining deadline.
comments: 2026-02-24 - Triage by Asha: labeled P0 because multi-region failover produced customer incidents last quarter (INC-559). Linked to ENG-6900 (reliability infra).

2026-02-28 - Design review notes from Priya (Platform PM): prefer default SDKs to be conservative (no hedging) but allow explicit opt-in via high-level client flags. Keep server-side hedging disabled by default in hosted mode until rollout safeguard is in place.

2026-03-03 - Eng sync: runtime changes required: deadline enforcement in router, KV cache TTL adjust, per-route shedder hook. Assigned to Miguel for runtime work, onboarding to compare with ENG-7124 (queue telemetry refactor).
2026-03-05 - Security review kickoff (notes in links): HSM-signed idempotency bits considered to prevent client forgery for enterprise flows; scope for runtime-2.5 if needed.
2026-03-08 - Prototype PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2012 - implements deadline header enforcement and a simple Idempotency-Key check. Awaiting tests. (Miguel)

2026-03-10 - SDK proposal posted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/456 - introduces RetryPolicy object and IdempotencyKey.generate_v2(). Reviews from SDK leads request clearer naming for hedging API. (CC @Priya)
migration_steps: 1) Publish SDK changes as beta, with opt-in hedging flag and default RetryPolicy set to 'balanced'.
2) Run runtime in permissive mode: accept new Idempotency-Key format but do not dedupe automatically; emit telemetry. (2 weeks)
3) Enable server-side dedupe for idempotent routes behind feature flag; monitor duplicate-side-effect metric and error budget burn (1 week).
4) Gradually enable hedging for internal customers and selected beta tenants using canary rollout in two regions. Monitor tail latency and cost per token. (2+ weeks)
5) Flip default hedging off/on decision after SLO verification; publish SDK stable release and docs.
qa_checks: Unit tests for deadline propagation and forced early rejection when deadline < 20ms.
Integration tests: two SDK clients (python/js) issuing hedged requests against a simulated slow replica; assert dedupe, correct status codes, and no duplicate state changes.
Chaos test: multi-region failover simulation with synthetic load to validate load-shedding and circuit-breaker behavior.
Load test: cost regression for hedging enabled on high-throughput embedding route must be < 3% increase in tokens-per-successful-response for tracked tenants.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Hedging increases token cost during spikes. Mitigation: hedging opt-in + per-customer budget guardrails and telemetry + automatic rollback on cost SLO breach.
Risk: Incorrect idempotency acceptance could block legitimate retries. Mitigation: permissive mode, accept legacy keys, and gradual enforcement with metrics.
Risk: SDK backward-compat break. Mitigation: keep default conservative, publish migration guide, and run compatibility tests across versions.
